definitions.informal: The evaluation is a total function from every candidate-property pair to a stance: with 24 candidates and 9 properties, the matrix is 216 stance cells, and n/a marks the pairs a candidate does not engage at its architectural level.
definitions.name: Stance mapping

definitions.informal: Stances form a preference order over postures — strong is strictly better than partial, partial than weak — while n/a sits outside the order entirely: it records non-engagement, not a worse posture than weak.
definitions.name: Stance order

definitions.informal: The six rungs are a total order, and the ladder carries one invariant: an agent exercising authority must have had it approved by an external principal — no rung lets the agent enlarge its own authorization.
definitions.name: Authority-ladder order

definitions.informal: Across an agent-to-agent delegation chain a to b to c, the trust the origin extends to the final delegate is bounded by delta times the trust of the intermediate hop: each hop may narrow the authority it passes, never widen it, so trust cannot amplify along the chain.
definitions.name: Delta-bounded delegation

definitions.informal: Layered controls compose as a single defense object: the eight mitigation classes act as one composed defense D rather than an ad-hoc stack of independent toggles, so the composition can be reasoned about as a whole.
definitions.name: Defense composition

definitions.informal: Each of the nine configuration invariants is a predicate over unreachable states: no agent goal may reach a configuration state that violates it. Authorization is enforced by making the violating state unreachable, not by trusting the agent to refrain.
definitions.name: Invariant predicate

definitions.formal_latex: L_1 \prec L_2 \prec L_3 \prec L_4 \prec L_5 \equiv L_6 \prec L_7 \prec L_8;\quad\forall i < 8\colon \textit{compromise}(L_i) \not\Rightarrow \textit{authority}(L_{i+1})
definitions.informal: The operating-system stack is an ordered defense sequence from hardware and firmware up to the agent runtime, with the container/microVM runtime and the update/provisioning layer as peers; the layering carries one requirement — a compromise at one layer must not grant authority at the next.
definitions.name: Stack layering

definitions.informal: A candidate's support window W is a fixed number of months or infinity under a rolling model; as the window is exhausted the risk of running the candidate grows, which is why the review treats an exhausted window as a posture change, not a footnote.
definitions.name: Update-window semantics
